MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
FIFTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
Principles of Computer Vision [CSE_3125]  
Marks: 50 Duration: 180 mins.  
PART-B  
Answer all the questions.  
1) Summarize the difference between the image processing and computer vision. Explain the (5)  
components of visual perception in detail.  
A  
) Course Outcome: "CO1"/ Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
B) Given a 1-D discrete signal and a filter, Apply both (5)  
correlation and convolution operations.  
Let the input signal and filter be:  
$$f = [0,0,1,2,3,0,0]$$  
$$w = [1,2,3]$$  
1. Perform correlation between fand w by  
aligning the filter to the input signal and sliding  
it across all positions (with zero-padding).  
o Show all intermediate steps.  
o Write the full correlation result and  
the cropped correlation result.  
2. Perform convolution between fand w by  
rotating the filter 180° and then sliding it  
across the signal (with zero-padding).  
o Show all intermediate steps.  
o Write the full convolution result and  
the cropped convolution result.  
3. Compare the two results and explain the key  
difference between correlation and  
convolution in this example.  
Course Outcome: "CO1"/ Cognitive Level: "Application"  
2) Define thresholding. Using the Global Thresholding (5)  
Algorithm, compute the threshold value T for the  
A) following 5x5 image (intensity values from 0 to 7), and  
show the thresholding result.  
Page #1

Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  B)   Illustrate the objective of the Canny Edge Detection technique? Apply each stage of the Canny          (5)  
  algorithm along with the mathematical equations used for edge detection.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3)        A mobile app that scans documents often captures images that are tilted or misaligned due to           (5)  
  uneven camera angles. Explain how geometric transformations help in adjusting the scanned  
  A)   image's position, orientation, and shape to achieve proper alignment  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  B)   An autonomous robot uses a camera to detect boxes in front of it. Due to lighting changes and        (5)  
  background noise, some feature points are mismatched, causing detection errors. Apply the  
  RANSAC algorithm to explain how it helps in building a reliable object model by eliminating outliers  
  and improving feature matching accuracy.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)        A smart traffic monitoring system records video footage at a busy intersection to track vehicles and   (5)  
  estimate their movement patterns. Apply the concept of translational alignment to explain how the  
  A)   system determines the direction and speed of moving vehicles across consecutive video frames.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)   You must design a real-time video denoising system for a CCTV surveillance feed running on             (5)  
  limited edge hardware (no GPU, low power, and restricted memory). The video suffers from noise,  
  compression artifacts, and moderate object motion. To perform motion-compensated denoising,  
  you must choose either dense optical flow or KLT-based feature tracking as the motion estimation  
  backbone. Analyze which method is more suitable for this application and justify your decision in  
  terms of accuracy, computational cost, robustness in low-texture regions or night-time scenes,  
  Smoothness across frames, and impact on object detection.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)        Apply machine learning-based approach to develop a tumor localization and classification technique (5)  
  for radiologists using MRI or CT images. How would you combine detection with medical image  
  A)   classification to reduce false negatives? Give detailed steps for the applied technique.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)   A large e-commerce platform wants to enable "search by image", where a user can upload a photo         (5)  
  of a product (e.g., shoes, bags, furniture) and instantly retrieve visually similar items from a  
  catalogue of 10 million images. Apply techniques of computer vision to develop a framework to  
  retrieve the most relevant images from the database. Provide description of the techniques in the  
  applied framework.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
